transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, um… I’m here because flying has become really hard for me. I know it probably sounds irrational, and I’m almost embarrassed to say it, but even the thought of getting on an airplane scares me so badly that my body just reacts like the plane is going to fall. I know that doesn’t make sense, but I can’t seem to shake it.
Is it just flying that scares you, or are there other situations that cause you similar anxiety?

It’s really mostly the flying. I mean… the thought of getting on an airplane now scares me so badly, and I know it doesn’t make sense logically, but my body just reacts like the plane is going to fall. I don’t think I have that same level of fear with other things.
Is your fear specifically about the plane crashing or is it also about being in the confined space of the airplane?

It’s more about the plane going down, I think. The confined space isn’t really the main thing. I know it sounds kind of unreasonable, but when I picture getting on the plane, my body reacts like it’s just going to fall out of the sky.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of flying?

About seven months, I think. It started after this really turbulent small-plane flight… around the time after I’d lost my clinic job. I kept telling myself it would settle down, but it’s kind of stayed with me since then.
Is your fear of the plane crashing focused on a particular part of the flight, such as takeoff, landing, or turbulence?

It’s not one exact part, I don’t think. It’s more… just the idea of getting on the plane at all. I know that probably sounds irrational, but my body reacts like the plane is going to fall, like it’s going to crash. Turbulence might make that thought worse, but the fear is already there before that.
Has your fear of flying affected your work, social life, or relationships in any way?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’ve tried not to let it become a big issue, but it has. I’ve turned down coverage opportunities that would’ve required flying, so that’s cost me some income. And I think a few colleagues have started to wonder if they can really count on me for those things, which is… embarrassing.

I’ve also missed some professional meetings I probably should’ve gone to, and I’ve put off seeing my family because getting there would mean flying. So yes, it’s affecting things more than I’d like to admit.
Are there any other specific situations, aside from flying, where you experience a similar level of fear or anxiety?

Not really… at least, nothing that comes close to that same level. I mean, I get normal stress with work and things like that, but not the kind of fear I get when flying is involved. If that makes sense.
Do you experience a similar fear when using other forms of transportation, like trains, buses, or boats?

No, not really. Trains or buses don’t do that to me. I might not love being stuck somewhere, but it’s not the same.

It’s really the airplane—the thought of getting on it. I know, logically, it doesn’t make sense, and I almost feel silly saying it, but my body reacts like the plane is going to fall. That’s the part that scares me so badly.
Have you ever had a similar intense fear of any other specific object or situation at any point in your life?

No… I don’t think so. Nothing that intense, anyway.

It’s really this one thing—the idea of getting on an airplane. I know it probably sounds irrational, and I understand logically that it doesn’t make sense, but my body just reacts like the plane is going to fall. That’s why I came in, really. It’s gotten bad enough that I can’t just brush it off anymore.
Do you think your fear of flying is something that you could be talked out of, or is it more of an automatic reaction that you can't control?

I wish it were something I could just be talked out of. I mean, I can tell myself all the reasonable things, and I know the statistics and all that, but it doesn’t really touch it.

It feels automatic. Even if I just get an email about a rural shift that would require a flight, my heart starts pounding right away, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe properly until I close the message. I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, but that’s honestly what happens.
